primitives.name: Play Indexing Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: SIGNALS 179 number the plays as follows: "Seven," full back buck on the right of center; "eight," full back to the left of center, and so on, to include all the varieties of attack that the team may learn all through the season.
primitives.assumptions: Each index corresponds to a unique tactical arrangement; playbook is finite and enumerable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Index collision or ambiguity when n ∈ {20, 30, ..., 90}.

layer2.mapping: Each play index n ∈ N maps to a permutation of player positions under fixed constraints, forming a discrete groupoid over positional space.
layer2.telemetry: Observable: successful execution rate of indexed plays.

primitives.name: Formation Signaling Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The tackle-back formation on the right can be called "formation A ;"tackle-back on the left can be called "formation B," and so on for each of the other formations desired.
primitives.assumptions: Formations are distinct and mutually exclusive; signaling precedes alignment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Signal delay or misinterpretation due to overlapping formation names.

layer2.mapping: Formation identifiers act as basis vectors in a tactical Hilbert space, where signal timing defines projection onto subspaces of valid configurations.

primitives.name: Position Change Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Formation signals, calling for changes from the regular positions, should be called before the men line up for the play after the preceding down.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Δx_i': 'displacement vector for player i', 't_s': 'signal timing', 't_l': 'line-up timing'}
primitives.assumptions: Players execute displacement within bounded time window t_s < t_l.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Execution failure when Δx_i ≠ 0 but t_s ≥ t_l.

layer2.mapping: Change protocol defines a temporal automaton over player state space, with signal events triggering state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Observable: deviation from expected position post-signal.
